title: Commercial LPG cylinders get costlier just before Diwali
body: Commercial 19-kg LPG cylinder prices rose in the big metros from November 1, 2026. Delhi went up Rs 10 to Rs 2,820, Kolkata up Rs 17 to Rs 2,971 (the biggest rise), Mumbai up Rs 10.50 to Rs 2,775 and Chennai up Rs 11.50 to Rs 2,994.50. The page ties the rise to Saudi Aramco's propane increase of 5.9% and butane increase of 6.8%. Household 14.2-kg cylinders stayed unchanged. The page warns that restaurants, hotels, tea stalls and caterers may be hit and food prices could eventually rise. It reports no direct public reaction.

title: November 2026 money changes: PNB card fees, IndusInd charges and local toll passes
body: A roundup of changes starting in November. PNB credit cards now charge no late fee on balances up to 500 rupees, but the maximum fee on balances above 50,000 rupees rises to 1,200 rupees. A 1% fee applies if utility payments exceed 50,000 rupees in a billing cycle. IndusInd Bank charges 25 rupees for failed POS or ATM transactions caused by insufficient funds on select savings accounts. Under a notification dated October 26, people living within 20 km of a toll plaza can buy an annual local FASTag pass for 1,500 rupees outside city limits or 3,000 rupees within them. The page reports no public reaction, and it says the PNB cash-withdrawal figures are garbled.

title: New airfare rules from January 2027 force airlines to show the full ticket price
body: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026 was notified on October 31 and takes effect January 1, 2027. Airlines must show the total payable amount at booking. That amount must match the ticket, with base fare, taxes, fees and cancellation charges itemised. The Centre can issue directions in an 'extraordinary situation', but there is no standing fare cap. The Supreme Court case on allegedly arbitrary and excessive fares is the backdrop, with a November 16 deadline for the Centre to place the rules before the court. The page reports no passenger or airline reaction.

title: Deepinder Goyal's Temple wearable opens India pre-orders at Rs 85,000
body: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal's health-tech venture Temple opened pre-orders for a head-worn brain-monitoring wearable, listed at Rs 85,000. The price reportedly includes a lifetime subscription, though the page says it isn't clear whether Rs 85,000 is the full price or an advance. Delivery is about three months after ordering, and refunds are available until the device ships. The Indian window was due to open at 9:30 pm IST on November 1. This page reports no public reaction. A separate Storyboard18 headline says the site crashed minutes after pre-orders opened.

title: Zomato's 'Have a WOW Diwali' campaign with Saif Ali Khan pushes restaurant hampers
body: Zomato launched a Diwali film with Saif Ali Khan pushing food hampers as gifts instead of towels, bedsheets and crockery. Khan reacts flatly to the household items and brightens when a Zomato delivery partner brings a hamper. The hampers come from select restaurant partners in four categories: mithai, assorted gifts, desserts and chocolates. The film was made in-house and posted on Instagram and YouTube. Marketing Head Sahibjeet Singh Sawhney said nothing beats a mithai-shop, bakery or restaurant hamper at Diwali. The page gives no figures and no public reaction.

title: Instamart's Diwali ad has a man wearing a chandelier to sell home décor
body: Swiggy's Instamart released a Diwali film that skips lit-up homes and family gatherings. A couple returns from a late-night party, and the husband appears wearing a crystal chandelier to exaggerate his tiredness. The film ends with an Instamart delivery and the tagline 'Diwali decor and more, only on Instamart'. Swiggy's VP Brand Mayur Hola said a man in a chandelier 'makes people look at the category'. The festive range covers linen, décor, cleaning supplies, electronics, appliances and beauty hampers, and the platform operates in more than 131 cities. The page reports no consumer reaction.

title: Ajay Devgn goes to Bombay High Court over FDA notice on Vimal Elaichi ads
body: Maharashtra's FDA says Vimal Elaichi commercials act as surrogate marketing for Vimal Pan Masala, a chewable tobacco product banned under state rules. Ajay Devgn challenged the show-cause notice in the Bombay High Court, calling it arbitrary. His petition argues liability should rest with the manufacturer rather than the celebrity endorser. Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff also received notices. FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said investigations into the three actors are complete and the matter will go to the joint commissioner for adjudication. The page carries no figures and no public reaction.

title: Gold and silver slip ahead of Dhanteras, but jewellery bills will still be higher
body: On October 30, 24K gold was Rs 1,43,668 per 10g (down Rs 666) and silver Rs 1,89,217 per kg (down Rs 5,716, or 2.93%). Dhanteras falls on Friday, November 6 and Diwali on Sunday, November 8. Buyers are weighing whether to buy now or wait for further falls. The page notes that making charges, wastage and GST push jewellery bills above the bullion rate. MMTC-PAMP's CEO Samit Guha expects demand to hold up, with smaller bars and coins and digital gold gaining appeal, especially among younger buyers.

title: Maruti NEXA festive discounts: up to Rs 1,36,000 on Grand Vitara
body: Maruti Suzuki announced October festive schemes across its NEXA range, including cash discounts, exchange and scrappage bonuses and pre-Navratri booking perks from October 1 to 10. The Grand Vitara Sigma petrol MT got up to Rs 1,36,000 combined. The Invicto got up to Rs 95,000, the XL6 up to Rs 61,000 for petrol and Rs 50,000 for CNG, and the e Vitara Rs 30,000 plus a free charger and home installation. The Baleno facelift got no consumer discounts. These are maximum figures that depend on trim and fuel type. The page reports no buyer reaction.

title: NPCI defers 0.4% UPI merchant fee until after Diwali after trader pushback
body: The 0.4% merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI payments above Rs 2,000 was due on October 15. The UPI Steering Committee said it will be implemented 'immediately post Diwali at a date to be notified separately', and no new date has been announced. The page's example is Rs 40 on a Rs 10,000 payment, with a cap of Rs 300. Merchant groups, trader associations and fintech firms had asked for more time during the festive season, and the page says the government worried about rising costs for businesses amid inflation. The fee falls on merchants, not customers.

title: Survey: six in 10 quick-commerce users say fees push festive bills above expectations
body: A LocalCircles study found Diwali shoppers on quick-commerce apps care more about value than speed. 71% want the best price or value, 65% want quality, 43% want low or no extra charges, and only 22% rate fast delivery as important. Six in 10 say delivery, handling or small-cart fees often make the final bill higher than expected. For last-minute festive shopping, Amazon Now led at 22%, Blinkit 19%, Zepto 14% and BigBasket 12%. Blinkit scored 5/5 for speed but 2.5 for value and transparency of charges. LocalCircles also said many households are holding purchases back until closer to the festival amid economic uncertainty.

title: Hero MotoCorp October dispatches rise 16% as festive demand lifts scooters and its VIDA EVs
body: Hero MotoCorp dispatched 7,34,403 vehicles in October 2026, against 6,35,808 a year earlier. Scooters jumped to 1,04,603 from 65,055. VIDA EV dispatches were 30,143, and its EV two-wheeler market share rose to 13.6% from 11.1%. Festive campaigns included Anil Kapoor and Ranbir Kapoor with the line 'Ghar Ghar Tyohar, Ghar Ghar EVOOTER'. Hero also launched the Xtreme 160R 4V and Xtreme 250R. The page reports no independent or customer reaction.

title: InnoData lays off nearly 550 employees in India, job cuts reported in the Philippines
body: Nearly 550 InnoData employees in India were laid off, per the article. InnoData has not confirmed the figure. Staff lost access to their official devices during the workday, and termination emails reached personal accounts later, with a termination date of 26 October 2026. Workers said HR never called them and they could not download payslips because payroll app access was revoked. One Delhi-based employee said, "One by one, we started losing access to our official devices." Nearly 500 people joined a WhatsApp group to trace affected colleagues. Some Reddit posts from the Philippines blamed a drop in work from a major client, but the article says these accounts do not confirm the scale or the cause.

title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees as AI leads to efficiency push
body: Microsoft offered voluntary exits to about 60,000 eligible employees in the U.S., Canada, India and the U.K. at level 70 or below. That is about 27% of a 223,000 workforce. Employees must decide by early December, and participants leave on Dec. 31. CNBC ties the move to AI spending: September-quarter capital expenditure is expected to exceed $50 billion, against $34.9 billion a year earlier. Chief people officer Amy Coleman called the offer "an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change." Some marketing, sales and engineering teams have reportedly decided not to take part. The article has no direct employee quotes and gives no India-specific headcount.

title: IT hiring takes divergent turns in Q2 as workforce numbers shift
body: In the September quarter, HCLTech added a net 6,450 people, ending at 2,30,339 employees. It took on 6,136 freshers, up from 1,056 the previous quarter. Infosys added a net 4,480, reaching 3,32,542, and its voluntary attrition fell to 12.7% from 14.3% a year earlier. TCS ended at 5,98,056, up 4,258, with trailing 12-month IT services attrition of 13.3%. Wipro's headcount fell by 6,716 to 2,36,328. Attrition is falling at several firms, which fits a cautious job market where people are staying put.

title: Wipro workforce declines 2.8% sequentially to 236,328 in Q2 FY27
body: Wipro's headcount fell from 243,044 in Q1 to 236,328 in Q2 FY27, a drop of 6,716 or about 2.8%. Net utilisation was 83.4%, against 86.4% a year earlier. Voluntary attrition in IT services was 13.8%, against 14.9% a year earlier. The company reported 212,663 employees covered by AI-ready workforce initiatives and 93,994 Master AI certification completions. The article carries no employee or executive quotes. It notes the data does not explain how much of the fall came from voluntary exits and how much from restructuring.

title: Indian Tech Salary Hikes Cool as Firms Prioritize Margins
body: Survey findings say about 35% of tech workers report either zero pay raises or actual salary reductions. Nearly 60% received increases of 5% or less. Employees at Zoho and Microsoft reportedly saw flat pay or limited adjustments, while Nutanix is cited as an exception with higher raises. The piece says employee priorities have shifted "from income growth to job security" and calls it "an unsettled workforce." It has no direct employee quotes, and the survey source is not named in the text I could verify.

title: AI Is Narrowing India's Entry-Level Job Ladder as 55% of IT Firms Cut Fresher Hiring
body: The article draws on the World Bank's India Development Update (October 2026), an ICRIER survey and a Nomura analysis. In the ICRIER survey of 651 IT firms, 55% reported lower entry-level hiring, against 25% at mid-career and 14% at senior levels. The six largest IT services firms' combined workforce is down by around 64,000 from about 1.7 million. The wider tech-services ecosystem, including GCCs, added roughly 700,000 jobs over three years to about 4.4 million. About 22% of India's employment is in a high AI-exposure category, versus roughly 60% in advanced economies. The article has no worker quotes, but the numbers point to a narrowing path for new graduates.

source: Naukri JobSpeak via The People's Board
title: AI/ML Hiring Jumps 20% as White-Collar Growth Hits 2%
body: The Naukri JobSpeak Index for September 2026 stood at 3,053, up from 3,002 a year earlier, which is 2% white-collar hiring growth. AI/ML hiring rose 20% and fresher hiring rose 1%. IT and software services fell 4%. Hyderabad grew 9%, while Mumbai and Delhi-NCR each fell 6%. The Rs 20+ lakh per annum band grew 23%. The split shows AI skills and senior profiles pulling ahead while freshers and mainstream IT roles stay flat or fall.

title: Festive cheer: Diwali bonuses and pay hikes across India
body: The Union Cabinet raised dearness allowance by 3 percentage points, from 60% to 63%, effective 1 July 2026. It benefits 48 lakh employees and 68 lakh pensioners, at an annual cost of Rs 10,016 crore. The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation announced a Rs 33,000 bonus for over 93,000 employees, Rs 2,000 more than last year. Goa sanctioned 30 days' emoluments, capped at Rs 6,908. In the private sector, MITS Group chairman MK Bhatia gifted four Kia Sonet SUVs to high performers, which the company calls an annual tradition. The piece does not report employee reactions.

title: Diwali 2026: BEST Employees To Get ₹33,000 Bonus; ₹75 Crore To Be Distributed On November 3
body: Mumbai's BEST undertaking will pay a Rs 33,000 bonus to each of its 22,654 employees. That totals around Rs 75 crore and is Rs 2,000 more than last year. The money is credited on November 3, just before Diwali. The article quotes BEST Committee Chairperson Trushna Vishwasrao and has no reactions from employees or unions. It shows how public-sector staff get predictable festival payouts that many private-sector workers do not.

title: Noida Labour Commissioner Dismisses False Claims of Diwali Bonuses
body: A viral message claimed the Supreme Court had ordered a mandatory ₹5,100 Diwali bonus, payable by November 5. Additional Labour Commissioner Rakesh Dwivedi called it "false and fabricated news, spread on social media by disruptive elements." Police registered an FIR. He urged workers not to protest over unverified reports. Statutory bonus eligibility needs at least 30 days worked in FY 2025-26, and the disbursement deadline is November 30, 2026. The fake message came nearly six months after workers' protests in Noida over a minimum wage increase.

title: Qualcomm layoffs 2026: Job cuts to begin in November, number of roles unclear
body: Qualcomm plans global job cuts starting in November 2026 but has not said how many roles are affected. It employed approximately 52,000 people globally as of September 2025. The article does not say whether India staff are affected and gives no functions, grades or offices. CEO Cristiano Amon said in a memo cited by Reuters: "We must have the right people in the right roles so they can perform at their best and the company can continue to succeed." The article carries no employee reactions, so the India impact remains uncertain.

title: Tamil Nadu plans weekly ethnic wear day for government employees
body: The Tamil Nadu government proposes a weekly day when government employees, including officers, staff and cabinet members, would wear traditional attire such as dhotis and shirts. It was announced at Tamil Nadu Day celebrations in Chennai. The stated aims are to boost demand for traditional clothing, support weavers and promote Tamil heritage. No start date has been announced. The article reports no reactions from employees, unions or weavers.

title: Two Indian creators shortlisted for Instagram's 2026 Rings awards
body: Instagram's 2026 Rings shortlist of 25 global creators includes two Indians: model Bhavitha Mandava and Kerala freestyle footballer Muhammed Riswan. The page says Riswan's viral street football clips have gathered millions of views and brand deals without big-money talent agency backing. Instagram reportedly chose honourees for creative risk-taking and community impact, not follower counts. The article says India's creator economy is 'clearly playing for keeps'.

title: Instagram tests long-form 'Features' video; Indian creators doubt it can pay
body: Instagram is testing 'Features', a longer widescreen video format, with a limited group of US users and some creators in Brazil. The page prints only 'November 2' with no year; the date is inferred from context. It cites more than 532 million Instagram users in India and says YouTubers earn Rs 50 to Rs 200 per 1,000 long-form views. Creator Larissa D'Sa says Instagram will struggle without clear revenue sharing. Divyanshu Damani expects creators to repost YouTube videos at first. Instagram's earlier long-form effort, IGTV, was discontinued in 2022.

title: Indian creators say Instagram takedowns are cutting their reach
body: SFLC.in recorded 268 content restrictions and 83 account restrictions across Meta platforms, X, Reddit and YouTube in October, a total of 351. Instagram had the most, with 174 posts and 59 accounts. Creator Raghav Trivedi (772,000 followers) had eight videos taken down in 48 hours, and his reach fell from 100 million to 30 million in October. Alpha Vishal said six of his videos were deleted and said 'videos with PM Modi's name are being deleted'. Amit Kilhor said he was 'surprised' that his pro-government reels were removed too. Creators fear that re-uploading deleted videos risks further restrictions.

title: Ahmedabad grocery store turns into a rave; Instagram splits
body: On October 27, youngsters danced to DJ music inside the Food Square India grocery store in Ahmedabad. Videos spread mainly through Instagram reels. The page gives no view counts. One user called it 'awesome', another asked whether rave-style sessions are allowed in a grocery shop, and a third asked 'What is even happening in Ahmedabad?'. One commenter joked that the city allows odd events like this but not alcohol.

title: Under-16 social media curbs: where Indian states stand
body: Foreign Policy reports that Goa became the first Indian state to consider Australia-style age limits in January. Karnataka announced a ban for under-16s about two months later, and Andhra Pradesh said in April it would draft a law limiting social media for under-13s. The piece cites about 500 million active social media users, 750 million smartphone owners and 'just over 1 billion' internet users in India. The page does not give individual public reactions. It is background for a live argument about kids, parents and screens.

title: Singapore Customs' Jailer 2 reel goes viral, Indian fans pile in
body: On 23 Oct, Singapore Customs posted a reel of its Chief General walking in slow motion down a jail corridor in tribute to Rajinikanth's character in Jailer 2, set to 'Hukum Reloaded'. It had over 142,000 Facebook views and over 57,000 Instagram likes at the time of writing. Rajinikanth fans from India crowded the comments, pleased that a Singapore agency knew the film. Others asked for a raise for the social media admin and praised the Chief General's 'auramaxxing'.

title: Bigg Boss Bangla 3 'jacket kiss' sparks 'family show RIP' backlash
body: After Nandini Dutta's eviction was announced, Rajveer Dey covered them both with his jacket and kissed her. She was sent to a secret room instead of being eliminated. Viewers questioned the show's family-friendly image. One post read 'Family show. R.I.P', another said 'Ashiqui 2 recreated in Bigg Boss Bangla', and another called it 'disgusting'. The page gives no viewership or engagement figures and quotes only five posts.

title: Jailer 2 opening day: fans dance outside theatres, milk on posters
body: Jailer 2 released on 15 October 2026. Fans gathered outside theatres in Chennai, Madurai, Thoothukudi and Tiruchirappalli to dance and sing. At Chennai's Rohini Theatre they poured milk on posters and performed aarti. The page expected at least ₹50 crore on Day 1, and related headlines cite a worldwide total above ₹750 crore by Day 14. Early reviews were mixed: critics praised the first half but found the second half weaker.

title: Fans angry that Mohanlal's Jailer 2 cameo was cut short
body: Costume designer Jishad Shamsudeen posted on Instagram that three of Mohanlal's looks were cut from the final film, including a scene shown in the trailer. He called the cuts 'simply unnecessary'. The trailer showed Mohanlal for only about two seconds. The page says the film was set to earn ₹100 crore on Day 1. Fans who went mainly to see Mohanlal felt let down. One user called Rajinikanth 'the insecure Superstar', and another asked Mohanlal to stop accepting guest roles.

title: Anirudh–Kavya Maran wedding buzz sets off Jailer memes
body: Reports about a wedding reception for composer Anirudh Ravichander and Sunrisers Hyderabad CEO Kavya Maran, reportedly set for November 21, sparked a wave of memes. Users joked that producer Kalanithi Maran was offering his daughter as the reward for Jailer 2's success, a nod to the Porsche Sun Pictures gave Anirudh in 2023 for Jailer. Others joked he could get Sun Pictures itself if Jailer 3 is a hit. The article says the jokes are 'purely speculative'.

title: Bhansali Productions trolled for Salman–Aishwarya Karwa Chauth post
body: Bhansali Productions posted throwback photos of Salman Khan and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan from Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam for Karwa Chauth 2026. Critics called it insensitive given the pair's past and Aishwarya's 2007 marriage to Abhishek Bachchan. The page quotes five X posts from October 29 and 30. One asked 'Are bhansali mocking salman here?', another called it 'raigbait', and another said it took 'serious guts'.

title: Karwa Chauth comedy skits dominate Indian feeds
body: This analytics page covers Oct 10 to Oct 29, 2026. It counts 314.4M social views (up 646% on a typical day at peak) from 409 creators (up 133%). The top video, by Chandrapal Singh, had 16.9M plays. Popular themes were husbands dodging expensive gifts, Mummy-versus-Papa arguments over the fast, and a 'festival scam' joke. Sentiment in 568 posts was 43% positive, 51% neutral and 5% negative. A few commenters objected to mixing up Karwa Chauth and Teej.

title: Drishyam 3 becomes Ajay Devgn's biggest hit as weekday numbers drop sharply
body: Outlook's page, dated 12 October 2026, says Drishyam 3 has reached ₹309 crore net in India and ₹479.80 crore worldwide. The opening day was ₹66.75 crore net, called the third-biggest opening ever for a Hindi film. Monday fell to ₹21 crore, a 65.6% drop from Sunday's ₹61 crore. The film is described as Ajay Devgn's biggest box office success. The article reports no audience reactions. Its numbers are set against the first film's ~₹110 crore and the 2022 sequel's nearly ₹342 crore worldwide.

title: Jailer 2 first-day-first-show reactions: Rajinikanth's swagger loved, second half divides
body: Sacnilk's 15 October 2026 piece collects reactions from the first shows of Rajinikanth's Jailer 2. Viewers praised his mass moments, Nelson's humour, Anirudh's background score, the interval and the cameos. They criticised the second-half screenplay, predictable writing, weak villains and pacing. In the ratings listed, 50.0% scored it above 2 to 3 out of 5, and 14.3% scored it above 4 to 5. Sacnilk cautions that this is a small selection of online opinions, not a consensus.

title: Jailer 2 opens huge in Kerala, but Mohanlal fans are angry over his trimmed role
body: Jailer 2 earned ₹12.50 crore in Kerala on day one. That is the second-highest opening day in the state's history, behind Empuraan (₹14 crore) and ahead of Leo (₹12 crore). All-India opening-day gross was ₹70.25 crore. Many Kerala fans said they were disappointed that Mohanlal's role was limited. Reports say scenes shown in the trailer were cut. Some fans accused the makers of shrinking his part to focus on Rajinikanth. His costume designer said three looks were removed and that he would not work on Jailer 3.

title: Nayyi Navelli opens at ₹3.25 crore with 'mixed-to-disappointing' reviews
body: Yami Gautam's horror-comedy made ₹3.25 crore net on day one, from 6,281 shows and 155,011 admissions. The Week calls the reviews 'mixed-to-disappointing' and warns that weak word-of-mouth could make commercial success harder. Evening shows and non-national chains helped the early numbers. Sacnilk later reported it beat Rajkummar Rao's Prahaar, ₹11.65 crore against ₹9.15 crore over the opening weekend. Both are small numbers beside the big films still running.

title: Ramayana: Part 1 advance sales compared with Adipurush, with caveats
body: Sacnilk's 22 October 2026 piece looks at advance booking 14 days before the 5 November release. Ramayana: Part 1 had ₹7.25 crore gross advance and 1.29 lakh+ tickets sold. Adipurush's final opening-day advance was 10.74 lakh tickets and ₹26.40 crore excluding blocked seats. Sacnilk says these are separate snapshots, not a like-for-like comparison. Sales are concentrated in Hindi, with early interest in Maharashtra and Delhi-NCR. Everyone is watching to see whether it avoids Adipurush's fate.

title: Matargashti on Netflix: a warm single-dad, teenage-daughter comedy
body: This is a five-episode Netflix series set in Lucknow, with episodes under 25 minutes. Dhara (Adrija Sinha), a studious teenager, plans to lose her virginity, and her single father Prakash (Rajesh Kumar) tries to stop her. The Hollywood Reporter India review, published 22 October 2026, calls it warm and watchable and not sensational. It praises its low-key, authentic take on girlhood and on a father and daughter who barely understand each other. Rajesh Kumar's gentle-giant dad is singled out. The page gives no viewer numbers.

title: Ramayana IMAX tickets average ₹1,500 against ₹380 for regular shows
body: OneIndia, published 25 October 2026, reports about ₹8.72 crore in India advance bookings for Ramayana Part One. IMAX is only 3.8% of shows but nearly 25% of advance revenue, with over 23,000 tickets sold across 140 shows. The average IMAX ticket is about ₹1,500, against about ₹380 for regular shows. Regular shows sold about 1.5 lakh tickets across 4,100+ shows, roughly 35 per screening. Hindi makes up about 87% of advance collections. The price gap is the obvious talking point for ordinary families.

title: A.R. Rahman's Ramayana song 'Mangal Rang' sparks debate over its qawwali sound
body: Gulf News, dated 26 October 2026, reports a debate over 'Mangal Rang', released on 25 October from Rahman's Ramayana score. Some listeners question whether its qawwali and Sufi-style sound suits a film on a Hindu epic. Others defend his freedom to experiment and compare it to 'Kun Faya Kun' from Rockstar. Rahman told Hindustan Times he focuses on the creative process, not online reactions. He called the work 'both an honour and a responsibility'.

title: Udta Teer opens soft at ₹4.10 crore, then climbs to ₹19.45 crore weekend
body: This page, updated 26 October 2026, covers Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan's spy comedy. Domestic opening weekend was ₹19.45 crore net: Friday ₹4.10 crore, Saturday ₹7.25 crore and Sunday ₹8.10 crore. Worldwide gross was ₹27.58 crore. Sunday occupancy was 25%. Sacnilk said the opening was about 83% below Ayushmann's best opener, Thamma (₹24 crore). The page calls the opening 'underwhelming' but a steady climb. The Hollywood Reporter India review is harsh, saying the film 'enters an endless loop of defeating itself'.

title: India beat Pakistan by 19 runs to win Asian Games cricket gold
body: Khaleej Times, dated 3 October 2026, reports India beat Pakistan by 19 runs in the Asian Games gold-medal match in Nagoya, Japan. India made 211-6, the highest total of the tournament so far. Abhishek Sharma hit 61, including a 20-ball fifty, and Tilak Varma and Shivam Dube added 62 in five overs. The match was played at a converted baseball ground before a small crowd. The page has no fan quotes. India-Pakistan matches draw heavy interest, and this was the first Asian Games meeting between the two.

title: India–West Indies series: Gill's 223*, Kohli's 15,000 runs, and a 2–2 T20I draw
body: The page gives match dates only; the last match, on 17 October 2026, was washed out. India won the ODIs 2–1 and the T20Is ended 2–2. Shubman Gill made an unbeaten 223 in the 2nd ODI, the highest individual score by an Indian captain in ODIs, and was Player of the Series. Virat Kohli's unbeaten 139 made him the fastest to 15,000 ODI runs. In the 3rd ODI West Indies chased 352 with Shai Hope on 162*. West Indies also chased 249 in the 2nd T20I. Fans were left talking about India's bowling in these chases. The page has no fan commentary.

title: Weekend box office: AK 47 beats Jailer 2 as Ramayana and Suriya's Scene near
body: Sacnilk, dated 2 November 2026, says Venkatesh's AK 47 led the 30 October–1 November weekend with ₹31.40 crore net. Jailer 2 followed with ₹26.40 crore, taking its 18-day India net to ₹456.30 crore (worldwide gross ₹807.25 crore). Udta Teer made ₹11.20 crore (₹42.10 crore after 10 days), and Drishyam 3 reached ₹377.35 crore after 31 days. The article calls the AK 47 and Jailer 2 contest much closer than the rankings suggest. Ramayana: Part One and Suriya's Scene arrive next.

title: FASTag annual local pass for people living near toll plazas starts November 1
body: From November 1, 2026, private vehicle owners living within 20 km of a toll plaza can buy an annual local FASTag pass. It costs ₹1,500 for plazas outside municipal limits and ₹3,000 for plazas inside them. The current monthly local pass is ₹360, or ₹4,320 a year, so the saving can reach up to ₹2,820 a year. The page says more than 13 crore FASTags have been issued. The page carries no commuter reaction. The only stated rationale is the road ministry's, which says the pass is meant to make regular travel more affordable for people near toll plazas.

title: Caller name display (CNAP) to go live on 4G and above from November 1
body: A DoT circular dated 13 October says caller name display must start on 4G and higher networks in all service areas from 1 November 2026. The name shown usually comes from the operator's subscriber record, unless the recipient has saved your number. Businesses may get a verified 'preferred name', such as a GST trade name. The page also lists spam-call rules, with AI/ML flagging of likely spam numbers and consent needed for transaction-support calls. It gives no customer reactions. The publisher sells telephony services and says some dates are its own estimates, so check the DoT notice.

title: Delhi bars non-BS-VI outside vehicles from November 1; NCR commuters most exposed
body: Under the Winter Action Plan, outside-registered vehicles that don't meet BS-VI standards cannot enter Delhi from November 1, 2026 to January 31. Delhi-registered older vehicles need a valid PUCC or they cannot buy petrol, diesel or CNG. AI-powered ANPR cameras at the borders will spot violations. The Transport Department estimates over 10 lakh NCR vehicles could be affected, including about 2 lakh in Gurugram and Faridabad and nearly 4 lakh in Ghaziabad. The article says people who commute from NCR cities for work or business will be hit hardest. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the rule covers petrol, diesel and CNG vehicles, including two-wheelers. No penalty amount is given, only a 'hefty challan'.

title: Urban India heads into Diwali with a smaller wallet
body: A LocalCircles survey of 67,000+ responses puts urban festive spending at ₹1.97 lakh crore, 6% below ₹2.10 lakh crore in 2025. The average household festive budget is about ₹20,000. 31% plan no discretionary purchase and 57% plan carefully. 83% expect to dip into savings. Amazon's no-cost EMI share is about 50%, up from 30%. Mumbai gold is about ₹1.5 lakh per 10g, against about ₹93,000 in April 2025. The article calls the mood 'cheerful on the surface and careful underneath', and says value retailers like DMart are gaining while jewellers' growth is mostly gold inflation.

title: Retail inflation jumps to 5.54% in September; onion prices up 108%
body: Retail inflation rose to 5.54% in September from 4.83% in August. Food inflation hit 7.74%, up from 5.97%. Rural inflation was 6.08% and urban 4.88%. Onion inflation was 108.09% year on year, ginger 62.85%, garlic 54.62% and lemons 36.41%, while tomato and potato prices fell. Restaurants and accommodation ran at 9.36%. ISB's Prasanna Tantri said on X that the RBI's low-rate stance is 'part of the problem' and that zero real interest rates cannot be sustained. The next CPI release is November 12.

title: RBI raises repo rate to 5.50%: what it means for home loan EMIs
body: On the day of the hike, the page worked out EMI examples assuming a 7.50% loan for 20 years rising to 7.75% if lenders pass on the full hike. A ₹20 lakh loan goes from about ₹16,112 to ₹16,419, a rise of about ₹307. A ₹30 lakh loan rises about ₹460, and a ₹50 lakh loan by nearly ₹767 a month. Actual increases depend on the lender's benchmark, spread and tenure. CSB Bank CEO Pralay Mondal called it a 'prudent step' because of inflation stress over the next few quarters.

title: 'Salary stuck in 2006, Bengaluru rent living in 2046': ₹22–24k for an old 1BHK with ₹1.5 lakh deposit
body: A Reddit user complained that a 15-year-old second-floor walk-up 1BHK in New Thippasandra/Indiranagar was listed at ₹22,000–₹24,000 rent with a ₹1.5 lakh deposit. The poster said private salaries seem 'beautifully preserved from 20 years ago' while landlords price rent for the future. Commenters mocked brokers' loose '1BHK/1RK' labels and being charged a month's rent for painting. One said Bengaluru needs rent regulation. Another advised asking for about 20% extra pay for Bengaluru work or moving to cheaper cities such as Nagpur, Bhubaneswar or Coimbatore. Another warned that high rent plus EMIs make a job loss dangerous.

title: Hundreds of online friends, zero in real life? Survey on lonely Indian singles
body: A Match Group–Ipsos survey of 1,000 singles aged 18–45 in metro and tier-1 cities found 35% constantly feel lonely, even though 75% go out to meet people at least once a week. 64% prioritise studies and jobs over social life, and 55% are too tired after work to meet anyone. 58% connect widely online but feel lonely offline, and 72% want a few deep connections over hundreds of casual friends. 40% use a dating app, 63% say apps reduced their loneliness, and 60% worry about safety. The page gives no outside commentary. The survey is commissioned by a dating-app company.

title: Commercial LPG at ₹2,810 in Delhi, domestic ₹942 unchanged since June; restaurants raising menu prices
body: The 19 kg commercial cylinder is ₹2,810 in Delhi, ₹2,764.50 in Mumbai and ₹2,983 in Chennai. The 14.2 kg domestic cylinder is ₹942 in Delhi and has been unchanged since June 7, 2026. The article cites crude above $108 a barrel and says a November revision is likely but not confirmed. Rural LPG refill gaps were cut from 45 to 25 days. Biometric authentication is mandatory for Ujjwala beneficiaries from October 1, or they lose the subsidy of ₹270–₹300 on four refills a year. Following commercial LPG spikes, many restaurants have raised menu prices, which the article says eventually reaches consumers.

title: UPI's new 0.4% merchant fee above ₹2,000: shopkeepers warn they may refuse UPI
body: As of 9 October, the page says a 0.4% merchant discount rate on specified UPI merchant payments above ₹2,000 starts 15 October, capped at ₹300 per transaction (reached at ₹75,000). Vendors receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month stay at zero. On a ₹10,000 payment the fee is ₹40. Transactions under ₹2,000 are over 96% of UPI merchant volume, per NPCI. A Chandni Chowk store owner said many of his payments exceed ₹2,000. The CAIT secretary general urged a rethink, and some Ghaziabad shopkeepers were considering refusing UPI. The page doesn't say whether the fee actually started. A later search snippet, not opened or confirmed, suggests the start was postponed, so check NPCI before posting.

title: Rules change from November 1: ITR audit deadline extended to Nov 21, pensioner life certificates, disability pension expansion
body: The ITR due date for audit-category taxpayers for AY 2026-27 moves from October 31 to November 21, 2026. Pensioners under 80 can submit life certificates from November 1 to 30. The Cabinet approved disability pension reforms on October 14, cutting the minimum disability threshold from 80% to 40% and removing the minimum age of 18. Monthly assistance is ₹375 for ages 0–79 and ₹625 for 80 and above, and beneficiaries rise from 8.33 lakh to 27.48 lakh. Guidelines are expected within three months, so it isn't yet operational. The page names only six of its 'seven' changes and has no public reactions.

title: GST registration made easier for co-working space businesses from November 1
body: From November 1, businesses can register for GST using a co-working address by uploading a membership agreement showing the location and desk allotted. Officials will skip physical address verification for Aadhaar-based registration unless fraud is suspected, and cannot ask for extra documents. Fraud notices must carry evidence, and unpaid dues alone don't count as fraud. The GST Council decided on October 8 and the circular is dated October 26. The page says small and new businesses and freelancers-turned-founders working from shared offices benefit most. It includes no statements from officials or businesses.
